name: Climate dynamics: partial-observation Lorenz-96 assimilation
description: Design an ensemble analysis update that reconstructs an evolving twenty-variable chaotic state from noisy observations of half its coordinates. The evaluator propagates the ensemble and compares each updated ensemble mean with independent high-accuracy reference trajectories.

sources.locator: Tomizawa and Sawada (2021), Combining ensemble Kalman filter and reservoir computing to predict spatiotemporal chaotic systems; Section 2.1 Eq. (1) Lorenz-96 dynamics and Section 2.2 ensemble data assimilation.

limitations: Synthetic deterministic twin experiments, not weather observations or the paper's reservoir-computing results.
Local reduced dimensions, seeds, observation noise, spin-up, perfect-model forcing and short duration are documented in the contract. Longer-horizon stability and forecast skill are not established.
All evaluation seeds are public. Use fresh seeds and forcing regimes after freezing the candidate for a generalization claim.

name: Climate dynamics: unresolved-tendency closure
description: Fit a shared degree-five polynomial approximation to the unresolved fast-scale forcing of a two-scale Lorenz-96 model. Train on supplied slow-state/tendency pairs and minimize normalized error on independent validation trajectories, including an unseen forcing regime.

sources.locator: Rasp (2020), Section 4.1 Eqs. (2)-(3), slow/fast model and closure target; Section 2 discusses offline versus online evaluation.

limitations: Local polynomial/offline adaptation with reduced K=8,J=4; not the paper's neural-network coupled-training protocol or a score reproduction.
Training and validation trajectories use distinct initial seeds; F=10 is absent from training, but all generators are public.

A deterministic local polynomial cannot recover every fast-scale tendency from the slow scalar alone. Lower offline error does not establish stable coupled forecasts or resolve cloud-feedback uncertainty.
